domain: Disaster Anthropology / Commitment Systems / Temporal Institutional Analysis
topic_summary: Analysis of the Aneyoshi tsunami stone's 'do not build below this line' directive across 78 years (1933-2011) of non-catastrophe, examining whether the kernel decayed to commemorative symbol or retained live behavioral commitment. The 2011 Tohoku tsunami provided a decisive test: Aneyoshi village survived while neighboring communities were destroyed, suggesting the commitment remained operationally live.

key_entities: Aneyoshi tsunami stone (physical marker erected 1933, inscribed with land-use prohibition)
Aneyoshi village (community that adhered to stone directive, survived 2011)
Neighboring coastal communities (violated equivalent directives, suffered catastrophic losses 2011)
1933 Sanriku tsunami (founding catastrophe that motivated stone placement)
2011 Tohoku tsunami (decisive test event, D5 catastrophe-theorem break)
key_tensions: Commemorative interpretation (stone as memorial/symbol) vs behavioral interpretation (stone as live land-use constraint)
Temporal decay pressure (78 years without catastrophe eroding commitment salience) vs institutional persistence (village maintained compliance)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The directive 'do not build your homes below this point' inscribed on the Aneyoshi tsunami stone, stabilizing a land-use prohibition grounded in catastrophe memory
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Authority derives from catastrophe witness testimony (1933 survivors) crystallized in physical monument; interpretive legitimacy contested between commemorative (symbolic) and behavioral (operational) readings

readings.expected_structural_delta: High epsilon—stone present but land-use decisions made independently; neighboring villages with equivalent stones built below line and suffered catastrophic losses; commitment decayed to ritual acknowledgment

readings.commitment: Stone as live land-use constraint—directive operationally enforced through community practice
readings.authority_grounding: Catastrophe-prevention pragmatism; stone authority derives from demonstrated protective function
readings.expected_structural_delta: Very low epsilon—stone directive causally determines settlement pattern; Aneyoshi's survival in 2011 while neighbors perished constitutes decisive empirical validation; commitment retained operational force across 78-year non-catastrophe interval

omegas.description: Does the 2011 tsunami constitute a true D5 catastrophe-theorem break (decisive test of commitment persistence) or merely a single data point? If neighboring villages had different stone-adherence patterns for reasons unrelated to commitment decay (e.g., topography, economic structure), the causal inference weakens. Comparative stone network analysis (deferred axis) would bound this uncertainty.
omegas.source: Kernel contest structure + deferred axis comparative_stone_network

omegas.description: What institutional mechanisms sustained behavioral competence across 78 years? Was it formal land-use regulation, informal community enforcement, property inheritance patterns, or catastrophe pedagogy? The temporal_decay_pressure axis identifies the challenge but not the solution. Missing mechanism may be a Rope (coordination) or Scaffold (institutional design) that warrants independent analysis.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + temporal_decay_pressure axis

omegas.description: Do the two readings genuinely emit different constraints, or are they observer-position differences on a single constraint? If commemorative_husk is merely 'behavioral_competence viewed by an outsider who doesn't see the enforcement mechanism,' the kernel contest collapses. The 2011 survival differential suggests genuine structural difference (Aneyoshi retained constraint, neighbors lost it), but this requires comparative_stone_network validation.

Did the 2011 validation event reset the temporal decay clock, or does the 78-year interval remain the relevant timescale? If catastrophe recurrence is the commitment-renewal mechanism, the next non-catastrophe interval begins in 2011, not 1933. This affects whether temporal_decay_pressure is a Rope (coordination challenge) or Mountain (generational forgetting physics).

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel contest structure validated: two readings emit genuinely different constraints (high epsilon decay vs very low epsilon persistence). The 2011 tsunami provides decisive empirical test distinguishing readings. Temporal_decay_pressure axis adds mechanism analysis without collapsing into either reading. Deferred axes documented for omega-level discussion.
